meta.title: Cearn Solar Farm: verified data sources
meta.project: Cearn Solar Farm, a proposed solar and battery storage scheme of up to 500MW grid connection on about 2,800 acres (about 1,133 ha) in three development areas around Garford, Charney Bassett, West Hanney, Goosey and Baulking, Vale of White Horse
meta.applicant: Cearn Solar Farm Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Telis Energy UK (Telis Energy Group; Protect the Vale states Telis was set up and backed by Carlyle)
meta.consenting_route: Development Consent Order (NSIP, solar over 100MW). Examined by the Planning Inspectorate, decided by the Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero. Vale of White Horse is a statutory consultee, not the decision-maker
meta.stage: Pre-application. No application documents published. Scoping information submitted; the Vale's response is due 23 November 2026. Submission expected September 2027 (checked 1 Nov 2026).

scheme.capacity: Grid connection offer of up to 500MW (developer says up to 143,000 homes). Programme Document states over 100MW
scheme.area: About 2,800 acres (about 1,133 ha) in three development areas. Not all would be panels
scheme.components: Solar PV, on-site substation, battery energy storage (lithium iron phosphate expected), collector compounds, access tracks, fencing, landscaping
scheme.grid: Underground cable about 12km north-east to National Grid's proposed Farmoor 400kV substation (also needed by Botley West). Cable route to be shown at Stage 2. The PINS boundary GeoJSON extends north-east towards Farmoor, so it appears to include the cable corridor
scheme.location_wording: South of Garford, east of Charney Bassett, north of West Hanney, south of Goosey and north-east of Baulking (PINS and developer)
scheme.land: Partly provisionally Best and Most Versatile. The amended Vale motion describes it as mostly Grade 2 and 3a
scheme.flood: Mostly Flood Zone 1, some parcels in Flood Zones 2 and 3 (River Ock and tributaries)
scheme.not_yet_published: Construction period, access routes, HGV numbers, compounds, working hours, operational lifespan, BESS size, community benefit amount, scoping report
scheme.community_benefit: Community Benefit Fund promised, value not stated. No shared ownership offer

links_to_reservoir.summary: Separate projects with separate promoters and decision-makers (Cearn: DESNZ; reservoir: Defra). Cearn is not the reservoir's solar relocation scheme. They are linked through cumulative impacts
links_to_reservoir.overlap_of_sites: Not established. Cearn lies north and west of West Hanney; the reservoir lies east of the A338. The Cearn cable corridor towards Farmoor could cross the A415 or A338 corridors near the reservoir; to be confirmed when the Stage 2 route is published (early 2027) by overlaying both PINS boundary files
links_to_reservoir.cumulative_assessment: Cearn's Programme Document lists cumulative effects with the White Horse Reservoir as a key issue, and the developer says it is in regular dialogue with Thames Water. Whether the reservoir's Environmental Statement includes Cearn is unknown; check its cumulative long list when published
links_to_reservoir.construction_overlap: Likely. Reservoir main works from 2029 or 2032 (Thames Water statements conflict) for over 10 years; Cearn construction would follow a decision around 2028 to 2029. Shared corridors probably include the A338 through the Hanneys, the A417 and the A415. Cearn routes not yet published
links_to_reservoir.who_has_raised_it: Vale Leader Bethia Thomas (23 Oct 2026), Cllr Sally Whiteman's council question on combined impact (about 5,000 ha), the amended Vale motion (cumulative impact with Botley West, West Oxfordshire Energy Park and the reservoir), Herald Series coverage quoting county and district councillors, and Protect the Vale (combined figure of at least 5,300 acres). GARD has not linked the two
links_to_reservoir.app_guidance: Show each project in its own section. Add a shared 'Combined impacts' page covering traffic corridors, construction timing, land take and the councils' cumulative-impact positions. Residents may oppose one project and not the other; letters and actions should be project-specific, with an optional combined-impact paragraph

council_positions.body: Vale of White Horse District Council
council_positions.summary: Motion on Cearn (proposed by Cllr Lee Evans) passed with amendments. As amended: solar should go on non-agricultural land first and avoid high-grade farmland; local shared ownership or benefit schemes and biodiversity gain; the Vale should not bear NSIP harms while benefits leave the district; cumulative impact with Botley West, the West Oxfordshire Energy Park and the reservoir must be considered. Resolves: Cabinet to develop a renewable energy policy and engage the developer on community benefits; Leader to write to the Defra Secretary of State and the OCC Cabinet Member for Transport. Vote and final wording await the minutes
council_positions.note: The motion asks for a letter to Defra, but the decision-maker for Cearn is the DESNZ Secretary of State

council_positions.body: Vale of White Horse District Council
council_positions.summary: Written answers: Cearn is decided by the Secretary of State; the council is working with the Oxfordshire Association of Local Councils so parishes can input; officers are taking a programme-wide approach to cumulative impacts through the Joint Local Plan
No Cabinet decision, highways response or motion on Cearn found
council_positions.note: Watch for the scoping response from OCC as highways and flood authority

council_positions.summary: Monitoring Cearn and attended initial events; no formal position yet. Its 2023 position paper wants Grades 1, 2 and 3a land avoided, rooftops and brownfield first, and treats cumulative impact as critical

how_to_get_involved.action: Scoping: the public cannot respond to the Planning Inspectorate directly. Ask your parish clerk and Vale ward councillor to press for specific items in the Environmental Statement: field-level land grades, viewpoints from village conservation areas, HGV routes avoiding villages, cumulative assessment with the reservoir construction programme, and battery storage siting and fire safety
Register for Planning Inspectorate email updates on EN0110044 and the developer's updates; write to the developer at info@cearnsolarfarm.co.uk or Freepost CEARN SOLAR FARM
Join Protect the Vale's update list; ask your parish to engage with the Vale's Oxfordshire Association of Local Councils route
Respond to the developer's Stage 2 consultation, the main chance to shape the layout and cable route. It is no longer a legal requirement but the developer says it will run it
Register as an Interested Party with a Relevant Representation on the PINS page within the advertised window. Only Interested Parties can take full part in the examination
Lobby the Vale and Oxfordshire County Council for strong Local Impact Reports; make written submissions and speak at open floor hearings

Write to MPs and councillors (see representatives) and to the DESNZ Secretary of State by post. Focus on planning matters: landscape, heritage setting, farmland grades, flood risk, traffic, noise, ecology, battery safety, cumulative effects
Judicial review in the High Court under section 118 of the Planning Act 2008, on legal and procedural grounds only (general information, not legal advice)

how_to_get_involved.note: The Vale planning committee and its speaking rules do not apply to Cearn because it is an NSIP decided by the Secretary of State
